items.reason: 'someone in that missing boat wore off that captain's best coat' reads as 'wore off' (faded/rubbed off); the sense is that someone went off wearing the coat. Readers and listeners will stumble.
items.new: "I will wager something now," whispered Stubb to Flask, "that someone in that missing boat went off wearing that captain's best coat; maybe his watch — he's so cursed anxious to get it back. Who ever heard of two pious whale-ships cruising after one missing whale-boat in the height of the whaling season? See, Flask, only see how pale he looks — pale in the very buttons of his eyes — look — it wasn't the coat — it must have been the —"

items.reason: 'what says Ahab?' is inverted archaic question form in otherwise modern sailor talk.
items.new: "His son!" cried Stubb, "oh, it's his son he's lost! I take back the coat and watch — what does Ahab say? We must save that boy."

items.reason: 'black seventy-fours' stops a first-time reader: the term is not explained anywhere nearby. Brief accurate gloss (ships of the line carrying seventy-four guns).
items.new: "He stood here this very instant; I stand in his air — but I'm alone. Now if even poor Pip were here I could endure it, but he's missing. Pip! Pip! Ding, dong, ding! Who's seen Pip? He must be up here; let's try the door. What? Neither lock, nor bolt, nor bar; and yet there's no opening it. It must be the spell; he told me to stay here. Yes, and told me this screwed chair was mine. Here, then, I'll sit myself down, against the transom, in the ship's full middle, all her keel and her three masts before me. Here, our old sailors say, in their black seventy-fours (warships of seventy-four guns) great admirals sometimes sit at table and lord it over rows of captains and lieutenants. Ha! What's this? Epaulets! epaulets! The epaulets all come crowding! Pass round the decanters; glad to see you; fill up, monsieurs! What an odd feeling, now, when a black boy's host to white men with gold lace on their coats! — Monsieurs, have you seen one Pip? — a little negro lad, five feet high, hang-dog look, and cowardly! Jumped from a whale-boat once — seen him? No! Well then, fill up again, captains, and let's drink shame upon all cowards! I name no names. Shame upon them! Put one foot upon the table. Shame upon all cowards. — Hush! Up there, I hear ivory — Oh, master! master! I am down-hearted indeed when you walk over me. But here I'll stay, though this stern strikes rocks, and they bulge through, and oysters come to join me."

items.reason: 'a vessel had been spoken' uses the period nautical sense of 'speak' (to hail/communicate with a ship at sea); a modern listener hears it as ungrammatical.
items.new: And now that, at the proper time and place, after so long and wide a preliminary cruise, Ahab — all other whaling waters swept — seemed to have chased his foe into a fold of the ocean, to slay him there the more securely; now that he found himself close to the very latitude and longitude where his tormenting wound had been inflicted; now that a vessel had been hailed which, only the day before, had actually encountered Moby Dick; and now that all his successive meetings with various ships had, in their contrasting ways, combined to show the demonic indifference with which the white whale tore his hunters, whether sinning or sinned against — now there lurked something in the old man's eyes that feeble souls could hardly bear to see. Like the never-setting polar star, which through the long, six-month arctic night keeps up its piercing, steady, central gaze, Ahab's purpose now gleamed fixedly down upon the constant midnight of the gloomy crew. It so dominated them that all their forebodings, doubts, misgivings and fears were forced to hide beneath their souls, and not sprout a single blade or leaf.

items.reason: 'He even seemed to doubt whether Stubb and Flask might not willingly overlook' is a double-negative construction that must be reread to see it means he suspected they might overlook it. Same hedge kept via 'seemed to suspect ... might'.
items.new: But when three or four days had slipped by since meeting the children-seeking Rachel, and still no spout had been seen, the monomaniac old man seemed to distrust his crew's loyalty — at least, that of nearly all of them except the Pagan harpooners. He even seemed to suspect that Stubb and Flask might willingly overlook the sight he was seeking. But if these suspicions really were his, he shrewdly refrained from putting them into words, however much his actions might seem to hint at them.

items.reason: 'not so quick, indeed, but that some of the flying bubbles may have sprinkled' is archaic 'but that' syntax that needs rereading. Rephrased keeping the hedge ('perhaps').
items.new: But the suddenly started Pequod was not quick enough to escape the sound of the splash the corpse soon made as it struck the sea; not quick enough, indeed, to keep some of the flying bubbles from perhaps sprinkling her hull with their ghostly baptism.

items.reason: 'But though thus contrasting within, the contrast was only in shades and shadows without' is a dangling participle with no subject; readers must reread to see 'within/without' refers to air and sea.
items.new: But though the two contrasted so within, without the contrast was only in shades and shadows; those two seemed one — it was only the sex, as it were, that distinguished them.

items.reason: 'the sun seemed giving' drops the infinitive in an archaic way.
items.new: Aloft, like a royal czar and king, the sun seemed to be giving this gentle air to this bold and rolling sea, even as bride to groom. And at the girdling line of the horizon, a soft and tremulous motion — most seen here at the equator — denoted the fond, throbbing trust, the loving alarms, with which the poor bride gave her bosom away.
